blocks.text: Chat Completions is OpenAI core text generation endpoint, applying the general request and response mechanics covered in the last two modules concretely to this specific provider, with its own particular endpoint path, parameter names, and conventions.

This topic covers the specific endpoint and request shape, the messages array in practice, common parameters, the response shape, requesting multiple candidate responses, and how Chat Completions relates to the newer Responses API, covered in the next topic.
1. Chat Completions as the Core Endpoint

blocks.alt: Building on the completed API Request and Response module, OpenAI APIs opens with Chat Completions

blocks.text: Chat Completions has long been OpenAI primary endpoint for generating conversational text responses, applying the request body and response body structures covered generically in an earlier module, concretely to this specific provider actual API.
2. The Endpoint and Basic Request Shape

blocks.alt: The chat completions endpoint accepts a POST request

blocks.text: This connects directly to HTTP methods and REST APIs, both covered in an earlier module, a request to this endpoint is a POST, sent as JSON, containing at minimum a model identifier and a messages array.

code.content:
import openai

client = openai.OpenAI(api_key=api_key)
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain recursion simply."}],
)

blocks.text: 3. The Messages Array in Practice

blocks.alt: system, user, and assistant messages structure the conversation

blocks.text: This connects directly to system prompts versus user prompts, covered in an earlier module, a system message sets persistent behavior, user messages carry the actual request, and assistant messages carry prior responses when maintaining conversation history, exactly the structure covered conceptually earlier now expressed through this specific API.
4. Common Parameters

blocks.alt: model, temperature, and max_tokens are common parameters

blocks.text: This connects directly to the request body topic covered in an earlier module, model selects which specific OpenAI model handles the request, temperature controls sampling randomness, and max_tokens caps response length, this specific provider parameter names match closely with the generic concepts already covered.

blocks.text: 5. The Response Shape

blocks.alt: A choices array, finish_reason, and usage make up the response

blocks.text: This connects directly to the response body topic covered in an earlier module, the response includes a choices array containing the generated message, a finish_reason explaining how generation ended, and a usage object reporting exact token counts, this specific provider response matches the general shape covered earlier closely.
6. Requesting Multiple Candidate Responses

blocks.alt: The n parameter requests multiple candidate choices returned at once

blocks.text: The n parameter lets you request several independent candidate responses to the same prompt in a single call, this connects directly to self-consistency prompting, covered in an earlier module, generating multiple candidates in one call this way is more efficient than making several separate calls to achieve the same effect.

blocks.title: This is a genuinely useful, often overlooked parameter
blocks.content: Rather than making several separate API calls to generate multiple candidate responses for a technique like self-consistency, the n parameter accomplishes the same result in a single request, worth knowing about specifically for this reason.

blocks.text: 7. System Message Conventions

This connects directly to system prompt design, covered in an earlier module, OpenAI convention places the system message first in the messages array, and it persists across every subsequent call in a conversation, exactly matching the general system prompt concept, expressed here as a literal message with the system role.
8. A Worked Complete Example

A complete Chat Completions call specifies the model, a system message setting behavior, a user message with the actual question, and explicit temperature and max_tokens settings, everything needed for a reliable, well configured request to this specific endpoint.
9. Chat Completions vs the Newer Responses API

blocks.alt: Chat Completions is the established endpoint, the Responses API is a newer alternative

blocks.text: OpenAI has introduced a newer Responses API, covered in the next topic, as an alternative to Chat Completions, offering some additional capability, Chat Completions remains widely used and well documented, understanding both gives you the full picture of OpenAI current API surface.
Worked Example

A developer building a customer support assistant constructs a Chat Completions request with a system message defining the assistant persona and scope, exactly matching the system prompt design principles covered in an earlier module, and a user message carrying the actual customer question, receiving back a well formed response with a clear finish_reason confirming the response completed naturally.

Checking the usage field in the response confirms the actual token cost of that specific call, letting the team track spending accurately against their budget, exactly the token cost tracking discipline covered in an earlier module.
Common Mistakes

items: Omitting the system message entirely and relying only on the user message to convey persistent behavior expectations
Not checking the finish_reason field, missing when a response was actually truncated by the max_tokens limit
Making several separate calls to generate multiple candidates instead of using the n parameter in one call
Confusing Chat Completions with the newer Responses API without understanding what genuinely differs between them

Key Takeaway

Chat Completions applies the general request and response mechanics covered in earlier modules concretely to OpenAI own specific endpoint, with a messages array following system, user, and assistant roles, common parameters like model, temperature, and max_tokens, and a response shape including choices, finish_reason, and usage, forming the foundation the rest of this module builds on.
